column1: # mapping_set_description: Manually curated alignment of the Mellea LinkML schema (linkml/src/mellea/schema/mellea.yaml) to the IBM ai-atlas-nexus AI Risk Ontology. Subjects are Mellea schema elements (classes and enum permissible values); objects are concepts from the ai-atlas-nexus schema modules (common, ai_system, ai_eval, ai_intrinsic, ai_capability, ai_aiuc, ai-risk-ontology). Mappings express conceptual alignment only -- the schemas have different modelling intents (Mellea = runtime/code architecture; ai-atlas-nexus = AI governance ontology).

column8: comment
Both are top-level container/catalog classes; semantics differ (code snapshot vs AI governance artifact bundle).
Mellea BackendSpec abstracts a model-serving provider; nexus AiProvider names the organisation/platform that provides AI capabilities.
BackendSpec instances configure a runtime AI system; nexus AiSystem is the deployed system itself.
ModelIdentifierSpec is the cross-provider naming of one model; nexus AiModel is the model entity proper.
Most ModelIdentifierSpec instances in mellea name LLMs; LargeLanguageModel is the corresponding nexus subclass.
ModelInfo (used in AiEval) records the model an evaluation was run against; overlaps with ModelIdentifierSpec on the identifier surface.
Both describe a LoRA/aLoRA adapter that augments a base model.
Mellea intrinsic adapters back what nexus calls LLMIntrinsics (capability primitives delivered as adapters).
Both enumerate the implementation kind of an adapter (lora, alora).
Mellea ComponentSpec names a stdlib component type (Instruction, Message, ...); nexus AIComponent names a component of an AI system.
A Mellea session orchestrates an AI execution; AiTask describes the task an AI is performing -- conceptually adjacent but not equivalent.
Name collision: Mellea RequirementSpec validates model output; nexus Requirement is an AIUC1 governance requirement.
Both express a constraint, in very different domains (runtime validation vs policy rule).
Sampling-loop strategy and nexus Action both denote an active behaviour pattern; weak alignment.
TelemetryMetricSpec describes a runtime telemetry metric; MetricConfig describes a metric used during evaluation.
Mellea telemetry feeds into observability; nexus AiEval is the offline evaluation analogue.
Plugins are pluggable runtime components; nexus AIComponent is closest available umbrella.
Hook payloads carry runtime observation data; nexus Fact represents an observed statement. Weak alignment.
ApiModelSpec describes HTTP wire models; nexus Input describes inputs accepted by an AI system. Surface-only similarity.
Formatters shape output representation; modalities describe input/output type. Weak conceptual link.
Mellea contexts carry conversational history; nexus lifecycle phases are higher-level AI lifecycle stages. Very weak link.
PythonPackage is a code-level entity; nexus Entity is the abstract root for all identifiable resources.
Both are the abstract root carrying id/name/description on every concrete subclass.
HuggingFace backend family corresponds to the HuggingFace AiProvider organisation.
OpenAI backend family corresponds to the OpenAI AiProvider organisation.
Watsonx backend family corresponds to the IBM watsonx AiProvider.
Ollama backend family corresponds to the Ollama runtime AiProvider.
AWS Bedrock backend family corresponds to the Bedrock AiProvider.
LiteLLM is a meta-provider gateway -- maps to AiProvider as the closest available concept.
Instruction components are inputs in conversational AI; nexus Input is the analogous concept.
Document components carry retrieval-style context; nexus Dataset is the closest available concept.
Intrinsic component category names the same construct as nexus LLMIntrinsic.
Same name collision as RequirementSpec vs nexus Requirement; runtime validator vs governance requirement.
Post-check hook outputs are conceptually adjacent to evaluation results, though emitted at runtime.
Generation post-call payload carries the per-call generation result; loosely analogous to an evaluation record.
Audit-mode plugins implement runtime governance checks; nexus RiskControl is the governance-side analogue.
